title: Critical Center Magnetization in the Planar XY Model
main_claim: Conditional on the companion inputs B, X, S (a(b_c)=8pi, the local RG maps, and the identical-nest center ratio limit), the aligned-boundary center magnetization at b_c satisfies a_n = A_XY n^{-1/8} (log n)^{1/16} (1+o(1)), with 0 < A_XY < infinity.

issues.location: sections/inputs.tex, Props inp:height, inp:partition-map, inp:balanced-map, Lemma inp:regular-variation
issues.description: The result is explicitly conditional. a(b_c)=8pi, the local maps and their parity-resolved quadratic coefficients (H>0, b=2 log L), the lower bound a_n >= c n^{-1/2} and the ratio limit a_{n'}/a_n -> d^{-1/8} are all imported from companion papers B, X, S. I did not re-audit those. The rank-95 sibling paper in this family depends on the same companions.
issues.evidence: 'Using the height, renormalization, and spin-field inputs from \cite{B,X,S} stated in Section 2 ...'

issues.description: I only spot-checked the analytic entry construction (smallness of the entry activity in the full analytic norm, and the polynomial insertion bound C_R s^{C_R}). The two-cell flow bounds (max |a_f| <= C/s, sum of a_f^2 <= C) and the cutoff error C(M/s)^2 e^{-c_1 s} check out. The tile and isolation estimates rest on adapting arguments from X and B, and I did not verify them line by line. Nothing I saw is wrong, but this part is unverified rather than confirmed.
issues.evidence: 'We prove the proposition by adapting the real-pattern and analytic estimates of [X, Section 5, Lemma 5.4], together with ... [B, Section 9].'

coverage: I read the introduction, inputs, trajectory, magnetic and terminal sections in full, read all of the bulk section, and skimmed the opening parts of preparation and entry. Checks I did: (1) The constants in the increment: E=(2pi)^2 G_n(0,0); the telescoped Green increment gives log L/(2pi) (Frullani gives log2/(2pi) per binary shell); the killed-square sine-sum formula for T_M is correct; -(1-t)/(2*8pi)*2pi log L = -(1-t) log L/8; with t=1/(2j log L) this gives 1/(16j). This matches the increment of log log n_j, which is 1/j + O(j^-2). (2) Marginality: lambda = L^2 exp(-8pi*log L/(4pi)) = 1, b = alpha^2 log L/(4pi) = 2 log L, and the fundamental charge gain is L^-2. (3) The sign of t>0 gives an effective height coefficient above 8pi and a positive log exponent. This is consistent with the KT flow and with the (log)^{1/8} two-point prediction. (4) The abstract separatrix lemma: the invariant-cone contradiction arguments, the backward solution for y = x - x*, geometrically separated jumps contributing O(1/j), and u = 1/(bj) + O(log j/j^2). (5) The common readouts are torus-size observables, so they depend only on the absolute index, which makes the overlap comparison between histories coherent. (6) The terminal error budget: D in [j^{1/10}, L j^{1/10}) gives D^2/j -> 0, D^4/j^2 = O(j^{-1.6}) and 1/(Dj) = O(j^{-1.1}), all summable. The evenness argument for wall supports gives O(1/(Dj)). The insertion residual poly(j) L^{-2j/3} e^{eps2 j} is exponentially small relative to a >= c L^{-j/2} once eps2 < log L/6. The rho_j and sigma_j cancellation is exact and needs no sign or size information. (7) The final step: the sequence B(n_j) has summable increments, and the subsequence argument transfers the limit to all n via the ratio limit. I found no step that fails.
sibling_notes: The family 216 board had one entry, for the companion paper 'The critical logarithmic correction for the planar XY model' (rank 95): no_gap_found. It independently confirmed the same increment calculation -(1-t)/(16pi)*Delta g -> -l/8 + 1/(16N), g_n = 4pi^2 G(0,0), and the separatrix u = 1/(2 l j) + O(log j/j^2). My checks of this paper's terminal and trajectory sections agree with that. It also flagged the same residual dependence on companions B, X, S.
